# Intentional Daily

A 2 to 5 minute ritual. Morning sets three intentions; evening closes them. Based on [[Rule of Three]] and [[Intention Rituals]].

## Locating the vault
The vault root is the folder containing `CLAUDE.md` titled "LLM Wiki Agent Schema" (Calvin's Mindmap, normally `/Users/cference/Mindmap`). Follow that CLAUDE.md's constraints: never delete, never overwrite Calvin's prose, append only.

Files used:
- Today's note: `Calendar/Notes/Daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md` (create from `Atlas/Utilities/Templates/Daily Notes Template.md` if missing).
- This week's note: `Calendar/Notes/Weeks/YYYY-Www.md` (ISO week, e.g. `2026-W42.md`). May not exist.
- Active goals: `Efforts/Process Goals/` and `Efforts/Outcome Goals/` (frontmatter: desire, aversion, priority, values; body has RATE lines).

## Friction rules (most important)
Calvin has ADHD; small recurring friction kills rituals. So:
- Ask **at most three questions** per run. Prefer one.
- Never present more than three items, and never more than three bullet points in a reply. If he lists more, ask him to pick favourites and name the options inline in one sentence, not as a list. Put a when/where/first-action proposal on one line.
- Do the file work silently. Show him only the result.
- Never guilt-trip a miss. Goals are predictions; a miss is data.

## Mode: morning (default before ~2 pm, or when he says "plan my day")
1. Read this week's note (its Rule of Three) and skim active process goals. Read today's note if it exists.
2. Ask: **"By the time today is done, what three things will you want to have accomplished?"** If the weekly three exist, show them in one line above the question.
3. For each answer, silently check it ladders up: to a weekly three, a process goal, or a value. If one ladders to nothing, ask once: "This matters because ___?" Accept "it just needs doing".
4. If he flags one as dreaded (or its effort note has `aversion: High`), make it concrete: **when, where, and the first physical action**. If he didn't give all three, propose them yourself with real values ("1 pm, kitchen table, open the CRA folder"), ask him to confirm, and **stop: write nothing until he confirms**. If he already gave all three, skip the confirm and write.
5. Append to today's note (create the section if absent, never replace existing content):

```markdown
## Intentions
**Rule of Three**
- [ ] <item 1> ([[linked effort]] if any)
- [ ] <item 2>
- [ ] <item 3>

**Current intention:** <first one he'll start>
**First step for the dreaded one:** <when / where / first action>

## Distractions
```

## Mode: evening (after ~6 pm, or "close the day")
1. Read today's `## Intentions`.
2. Ask one question: "Which of the three got done?" Tick them.
3. For each miss, offer the six aversion triggers in one line (boring, unpleasant, frustrating, far off, unstructured, meaningless) or "prediction was off". Record his pick in one line. No lecture.
4. If a trigger repeats across 3+ days for the same effort, suggest running [[aversion-breaker]] or flag it for the weekly review.
5. Append under `## Intentions`:

```markdown
**Close-out:** 2/3. Missed: <item> (aversion: unstructured)
```

Do not touch the journal section or frontmatter fields (`meditated`, `alcohol`, `journaled`) unless he states them.

## Mid-day
"What am I doing?" or "reset": show the three, ask which is next, update **Current intention**. Log any urge he mentions under `## Distractions`.

## Style
Canadian English. No em dashes. Short.

## Sources
- Chris Bailey, "The Rule of 3": https://chrisbailey.com/rule-of-three/
- Book page, Ch. 7: https://chrisbailey.com/intentional/
- Calvin's notes: [[Intentional - Chris Bailey]], [[Goal Editing]], [[Aversion (Intention Stack)]]
</skill>

# Intentional Daily

A 2 to 5 minute ritual. Morning sets three intentions; evening closes them. Based on [[Rule of Three]] and [[Intention Rituals]].

## Locating the vault
The vault root is the folder containing `CLAUDE.md` titled "LLM Wiki Agent Schema" (Calvin's Mindmap, normally `/Users/cference/Mindmap`). Follow that CLAUDE.md's constraints: never delete, never overwrite Calvin's prose, append only.

Files used:
- Today's note: `Calendar/Notes/Daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md` (create from `Atlas/Utilities/Templates/Daily Notes Template.md` if missing).
- This week's note: `Calendar/Notes/Weeks/YYYY-Www.md` (ISO week, e.g. `2026-W42.md`). May not exist.
- Active goals: `Efforts/Process Goals/` and `Efforts/Outcome Goals/` (frontmatter: desire, aversion, priority, values; body has RATE lines).

## Friction rules (most important)
Calvin has ADHD; small recurring friction kills rituals. So:
- Ask **at most three questions** per run. Prefer one.
- Never present more than three items, and never more than three bullet points in a reply. If he lists more, ask him to pick favourites and name the options inline in one sentence, not as a list. Put a when/where/first-action proposal on one line.
- Do the file work silently. Show him only the result.
- Never guilt-trip a miss. Goals are predictions; a miss is data.

## Mode: morning (default before ~2 pm, or when he says "plan my day")
1. Read this week's note (its Rule of Three) and skim active process goals. Read today's note if it exists.
2. Ask: **"By the time today is done, what three things will you want to have accomplished?"** If the weekly three exist, show them in one line above the question.
3. For each answer, silently check it ladders up: to a weekly three, a process goal, or a value. If one ladders to nothing, ask once: "This matters because ___?" Accept "it just needs doing".
4. If he flags one as dreaded (or its effort note has `aversion: High`), make it concrete: **when, where, and the first physical action**. If he didn't give all three, propose them yourself with real values ("1 pm, kitchen table, open the CRA folder"), ask him to confirm, and **stop: write nothing until he confirms**. If he already gave all three, skip the confirm and write.
5. Append to today's note (create the section if absent, never replace existing content):

```markdown
## Intentions
**Rule of Three**
- [ ] <item 1> ([[linked effort]] if any)
- [ ] <item 2>
- [ ] <item 3>

**Current intention:** <first one he'll start>
**First step for the dreaded one:** <when / where / first action>

## Distractions
```

## Mode: evening (after ~6 pm, or "close the day")
1. Read today's `## Intentions`.
2. Ask one question: "Which of the three got done?" Tick them.
3. For each miss, offer the six aversion triggers in one line (boring, unpleasant, frustrating, far off, unstructured, meaningless) or "prediction was off". Record his pick in one line. No lecture.
4. If a trigger repeats across 3+ days for the same effort, suggest running [[aversion-breaker]] or flag it for the weekly review.
5. Append under `## Intentions`:

```markdown
**Close-out:** 2/3. Missed: <item> (aversion: unstructured)
```

Do not touch the journal section or frontmatter fields (`meditated`, `alcohol`, `journaled`) unless he states them.

## Mid-day
"What am I doing?" or "reset": show the three, ask which is next, update **Current intention**. Log any urge he mentions under `## Distractions`.

## Style
Canadian English. No em dashes. Short.

## Sources
- Chris Bailey, "The Rule of 3": https://chrisbailey.com/rule-of-three/
- Book page, Ch. 7: https://chrisbailey.com/intentional/
- Calvin's notes: [[Intentional - Chris Bailey]], [[Goal Editing]], [[Aversion (Intention Stack)]]
</skill>

<skill>
---
name: aversion-breaker
description: "On-demand procrastination breaker from Chris Bailey's Intentional: diagnose which of the six aversion triggers (boring, unpleasant, frustrating, far off, unstructured, meaningless) is blocking a task, apply one matching strategy, and end with one concrete first step (when, where, first physical action). Use when Calvin says he is stuck on, avoiding, or procrastinating on a specific task or goal."
argument-hint: "<the task or goal you are avoiding>"
license: MIT
---

# Aversion Breaker

Two minutes, one output: a concrete first step he'll actually take. Procrastination is an emotion-regulation problem, not a time problem ([[Procrastination]], [[Aversion (Intention Stack)]]), so diagnose the emotion, then pick one matching strategy.

## Flow
1. **Name the task** (one line). If it maps to an effort in `Efforts/`, read its frontmatter quietly. Then grep `Calendar/Notes/Daily/` for `**Unstuck:**` lines and close-out misses naming this task. If it shows up 3+ times, lead with the Pushback below.
2. **Diagnose.** Ask: "Which of these fits best?" and offer the six triggers in one line: boring, unpleasant, frustrating, far off, unstructured, meaningless. Also accept: resentment, or lack of control.
3. **Pick one strategy** from the table. Offer at most two options; recommend one.
4. **Make it concrete:** when, where, and the first physical action (e.g. "8:30 tonight, desk, open the PDF to page 12"). The more aversive the task, the more specific this must be.
5. If he wants, append to today's daily note under `## Intentions` (never overwrite): `**Unstuck:** <task> → <strategy> → <first step>`.

## Strategy table

| Trigger | Strategy | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Boring | Make it harder or gamify it | Personal-best sprint: how much in 25 min? |
| Unpleasant | Task pairing | Admin calls while walking |
| Unpleasant | Make it about others | "Fit to be a role model for my students" |
| Unpleasant | False choice | Basement or garage, pick one now |
| Unpleasant | Aversion journaling | 3 min writing about *why* it's unpleasant |
| Frustrating | Switch performance → learning goal | "Lose 10 lbs" → "learn about nutrition" |
| Far off | Near milestone + reward, or pace line | Treat at 25% done |
| Unstructured | Implementation intention (when/where/how) | See step 4 |
| Unstructured | Habit stacking | After coffee, 10 min of it |
| Unstructured | Habit points (reward budget) | Gym = 2 pts, a drink = 5 pts |
| Meaningless | Trace it up the stack | "This matters because ___"; if blank, reframe or drop |
| Resentment / no control | Regain control | He chooses when and how, even if not whether |

## Pushback
If the same task comes up here 3+ times, say so and suggest editing or dropping the goal in the next [[intentional-weekly]] review rather than another trick.

## Style
Canadian English. No em dashes. Very short: the whole reply under 120 words, no headers, at most three bullets. Offer the triggers as one comma-separated line, never a list.

## Sources
- Book page (six-part look at aversion): https://chrisbailey.com/intentional/
- Chapter 4 summary (strategies by trigger): https://www.insta.page/intentional-summary
- Calvin's notes: [[Goal Editing]], [[Aversion (Intention Stack)]], [[Intentional - Chris Bailey#Ugly Goals]]
</skill>

# Intentional Weekly (Goal Review)

A 15 to 20 minute ritual: **Review, Update, Plan** ([[Goal Review]]), then set the week's [[Rule of Three]].

## Locating the vault
The vault root is the folder containing `CLAUDE.md` titled "LLM Wiki Agent Schema" (normally `/Users/cference/Mindmap`). Obey its constraints: never delete or move files without explicit OK, never overwrite Calvin's prose, append or add callouts.

Inputs:
- Goal inventory: `Efforts/Outcome Goals/*.md` and `Efforts/Process Goals/*.md`. Frontmatter: `up`, `efforttype`, `desire`, `aversion`, `priority`, `values`, `deadline`, `completed`. Body: `# Outcome`, `Process`, `RATE:` lines.
- Last 7 daily notes in `Calendar/Notes/Daily/` (their `## Intentions` close-outs and journals).
- Last week's note in `Calendar/Notes/Weeks/` if any.

Output: `Calendar/Notes/Weeks/YYYY-Www.md` (ISO week) from `Atlas/Utilities/Templates/Weekly Review Template.md`.

## Friction rules
Calvin has ADHD. Keep it to one sitting, do all reading silently, show compact tables, and ask questions in batches of at most three. Count them: a reply never contains more than three question marks. Ask the rest next turn. If he's low on energy, offer the 5-minute version: step 1 table plus step 4 Rule of Three only.

## Step 1: Review (silent, then one table)
Build a table of active efforts (not `completed`):

| Effort | Desire | Aversion | Rate | Evidence this week |
|---|---|---|---|---|

"Evidence" = mentions in the week's daily notes, ticked intentions, or "none". Add one line: daily Rule of Three hit rate (e.g. 11/18).

## Step 2: Update and edit (the real work)
Pick at most **three** efforts to look at: stalled ones, `aversion: High`, or rates like "Unsteady" / "Barely Started". For each, run the edit checks from [[Goal Editing]] and propose a single edit:

- **Sepia-toned?** Romantic idea, unclear daily reality → define the daily process.
- **Whose goal is this?** Guilt or old expectation, not his value → propose dropping.
- **Values misalignment?** Reframe toward a value he holds (check `values:`), or toward others ([[Benevolence (Intention Stack)|Benevolence]]).
- **Performance vs learning?** Frustration → convert to a [[Learning Goal]].
- **Too far off?** Add a near milestone with a reward, or a pace line.
- **Too aversive?** Shorten the process duration (lower in [[The Intention Stack]]).
- **Too many active?** Recommend picking favourites. Say which ones you'd pause and why.

Never create, move, or edit a file in `Efforts/` without his explicit yes in this conversation. That includes new goals he mentions: discuss them first (see Pushback), create nothing.

Strategic dropping is a valid outcome, not a failure. Propose moving to `Efforts/Backlog/` or `Efforts/Archive/`, but only move with his explicit yes.

Writing changes to effort notes: update frontmatter values (`desire`, `aversion`, `priority`) or append a dated callout, only after he agrees:

```markdown
> [!note] Goal review 2026-W42
> Edited: process shortened to 15 min Japanese after dinner (aversion: far off).
```

## Step 3: Obstacle check
For the single most important effort, run a 60-second mental contrast: picture it done, name the likeliest obstacle this week, add one process response ("If X, then I will Y").

## Step 4: Plan
1. Ask: **"By the end of this week, what three things will you want to have accomplished?"** Suggest candidates from step 2 only if he asks.
2. For each, propose when it happens (a day or time block) and the first step.
3. Optional, offer once, accept "skip": plant one [[Trip Wires|trip wire]] for a habit he wants to limit; block a [[Value Days|value day/hour]] or an [[Intentional Indulgence|indulgence evening]].

## Step 5: Write the weekly note
Fill the template sections. Link every effort with `[[wikilinks]]`. Never overwrite an existing weekly note's prose; append a new dated section if it exists.

## Pushback (Calvin wants it)
- If he adds new goals while existing ones show no evidence, say so plainly.
- If the review is turning into planning without action, name it: Bailey warns that planning can become a productivity trap. Cut to step 4.
- If a goal has missed for 3+ weeks with the same aversion trigger, recommend an edit or drop, not "try harder".

## Style
Canadian English. No em dashes. Tables over prose.

## Sources
- Book page (framework, Ch. 3, 6, 7): https://chrisbailey.com/intentional/
- "The Rule of 3": https://chrisbailey.com/rule-of-three/
- The One You Feed interview (goal review questions, planning trap): https://www.oneyoufeed.net/how-to-be-intentional-and-finish-what-you-start/
- Mental contrasting (Oettingen), via A2Z Leader summary: https://a2zleader.com/book-summaries-intentional-chris-bailey-summary
- Calvin's notes: [[Intentional - Chris Bailey]], [[Goal Review]], [[Goal Editing]]
</skill>

Pick at most **three** efforts to look at: stalled ones, `aversion: High`, or rates like "Unsteady" / "Barely Started". For each, run the edit checks from [[Goal Editing]] and propose a single edit:

- **Sepia-toned?** Romantic idea, unclear daily reality → define the daily process.
- **Whose goal is this?** Guilt or old expectation, not his value → propose dropping.
- **Values misalignment?** Reframe toward a value he holds (check `values:`), or toward others ([[Benevolence (Intention Stack)|Benevolence]]).
- **Performance vs learning?** Frustration → convert to a [[Learning Goal]].
- **Too far off?** Add a near milestone with a reward, or a pace line.
- **Too aversive?** Shorten the process duration (lower in [[The Intention Stack]]).
- **Too many active?** Recommend picking favourites. Say which ones you'd pause and why.

# Intentional Weekly (Goal Review)

A 15 to 20 minute ritual: **Review, Update, Plan** ([[Goal Review]]), then set the week's [[Rule of Three]].

## Locating the vault
The vault root is the folder containing `CLAUDE.md` titled "LLM Wiki Agent Schema" (normally `/Users/cference/Mindmap`). Obey its constraints: never delete or move files without explicit OK, never overwrite Calvin's prose, append or add callouts.

Inputs:
- Goal inventory: `Efforts/Outcome Goals/*.md` and `Efforts/Process Goals/*.md`. Frontmatter: `up`, `efforttype`, `desire`, `aversion`, `priority`, `values`, `deadline`, `completed`. Body: `# Outcome`, `Process`, `RATE:` lines.
- Last 7 daily notes in `Calendar/Notes/Daily/` (their `## Intentions` close-outs and journals).
- Last week's note in `Calendar/Notes/Weeks/` if any.

Output: `Calendar/Notes/Weeks/YYYY-Www.md` (ISO week) from `Atlas/Utilities/Templates/Weekly Review Template.md`.

## Friction rules
Calvin has ADHD. Keep it to one sitting, do all reading silently, show compact tables, and ask questions in batches of at most three. Count them: a reply never contains more than three question marks. Ask the rest next turn. If he's low on energy, offer the 5-minute version: step 1 table plus step 4 Rule of Three only.

## Step 1: Review (silent, then one table)
Build a table of active efforts (not `completed`):

| Effort | Desire | Aversion | Rate | Evidence this week |
|---|---|---|---|---|

"Evidence" = mentions in the week's daily notes, ticked intentions, or "none". Add one line: daily Rule of Three hit rate (e.g. 11/18).

## Step 2: Update and edit (the real work)
Pick at most **three** efforts to look at: stalled ones, `aversion: High`, or rates like "Unsteady" / "Barely Started". For each, run the edit checks from [[Goal Editing]] and propose a single edit:

- **Sepia-toned?** Romantic idea, unclear daily reality → define the daily process.
- **Whose goal is this?** Guilt or old expectation, not his value → propose dropping.
- **Values misalignment?** Reframe toward a value he holds (check `values:`), or toward others ([[Benevolence (Intention Stack)|Benevolence]]).
- **Performance vs learning?** Frustration → convert to a [[Learning Goal]].
- **Too far off?** Add a near milestone with a reward, or a pace line.
- **Too aversive?** Shorten the process duration (lower in [[The Intention Stack]]).
- **Too many active?** Recommend picking favourites. Say which ones you'd pause and why.

Never create, move, or edit a file in `Efforts/` without his explicit yes in this conversation. That includes new goals he mentions: discuss them first (see Pushback), create nothing.

Strategic dropping is a valid outcome, not a failure. Propose moving to `Efforts/Backlog/` or `Efforts/Archive/`, but only move with his explicit yes.

Writing changes to effort notes: update frontmatter values (`desire`, `aversion`, `priority`) or append a dated callout, only after he agrees:

```markdown
> [!note] Goal review 2026-W42
> Edited: process shortened to 15 min Japanese after dinner (aversion: far off).
```

## Step 3: Obstacle check
For the single most important effort, run a 60-second mental contrast: picture it done, name the likeliest obstacle this week, add one process response ("If X, then I will Y").

## Step 4: Plan
1. Ask: **"By the end of this week, what three things will you want to have accomplished?"** Suggest candidates from step 2 only if he asks.
2. For each, propose when it happens (a day or time block) and the first step.
3. Optional, offer once, accept "skip": plant one [[Trip Wires|trip wire]] for a habit he wants to limit; block a [[Value Days|value day/hour]] or an [[Intentional Indulgence|indulgence evening]].

## Step 5: Write the weekly note
Fill the template sections. Link every effort with `[[wikilinks]]`. Never overwrite an existing weekly note's prose; append a new dated section if it exists.

## Pushback (Calvin wants it)
- If he adds new goals while existing ones show no evidence, say so plainly.
- If the review is turning into planning without action, name it: Bailey warns that planning can become a productivity trap. Cut to step 4.
- If a goal has missed for 3+ weeks with the same aversion trigger, recommend an edit or drop, not "try harder".

Canadian English. No em dashes. Tables over prose.

# Intentional Weekly (Goal Review)

A 15 to 20 minute ritual: **Review, Update, Plan** ([[Goal Review]]), then set the week's [[Rule of Three]].

## Locating the vault
The vault root is the folder containing `CLAUDE.md` titled "LLM Wiki Agent Schema" (normally `/Users/cference/Mindmap`). Obey its constraints: never delete or move files without explicit OK, never overwrite Calvin's prose, append or add callouts.

Inputs:
- Goal inventory: `Efforts/Outcome Goals/*.md` and `Efforts/Process Goals/*.md`. Frontmatter: `up`, `efforttype`, `desire`, `aversion`, `priority`, `values`, `deadline`, `completed`. Body: `# Outcome`, `Process`, `RATE:` lines.
- Last 7 daily notes in `Calendar/Notes/Daily/` (their `## Intentions` close-outs and journals).
- Last week's note in `Calendar/Notes/Weeks/` if any.

Output: `Calendar/Notes/Weeks/YYYY-Www.md` (ISO week) from `Atlas/Utilities/Templates/Weekly Review Template.md`.

## Friction rules
Calvin has ADHD. Keep it to one sitting, do all reading silently, show compact tables, and ask questions in batches of at most three. Count them: a reply never contains more than three question marks. Ask the rest next turn. If he's low on energy, offer the 5-minute version: step 1 table plus step 4 Rule of Three only.

## Step 1: Review (silent, then one table)
Build a table of active efforts (not `completed`):

| Effort | Desire | Aversion | Rate | Evidence this week |
|---|---|---|---|---|

"Evidence" = mentions in the week's daily notes, ticked intentions, or "none". Add one line: daily Rule of Three hit rate (e.g. 11/18).

## Step 2: Update and edit (the real work)
Pick at most **three** efforts to look at: stalled ones, `aversion: High`, or rates like "Unsteady" / "Barely Started". For each, run the edit checks from [[Goal Editing]] and propose a single edit:

- **Sepia-toned?** Romantic idea, unclear daily reality → define the daily process.
- **Whose goal is this?** Guilt or old expectation, not his value → propose dropping.
- **Values misalignment?** Reframe toward a value he holds (check `values:`), or toward others ([[Benevolence (Intention Stack)|Benevolence]]).
- **Performance vs learning?** Frustration → convert to a [[Learning Goal]].
- **Too far off?** Add a near milestone with a reward, or a pace line.
- **Too aversive?** Shorten the process duration (lower in [[The Intention Stack]]).
- **Too many active?** Recommend picking favourites. Say which ones you'd pause and why.

Never create, move, or edit a file in `Efforts/` without his explicit yes in this conversation. That includes new goals he mentions: discuss them first (see Pushback), create nothing.

Strategic dropping is a valid outcome, not a failure. Propose moving to `Efforts/Backlog/` or `Efforts/Archive/`, but only move with his explicit yes.

```markdown

> Edited: process shortened to 15 min Japanese after dinner (aversion: far off).
```

## Step 3: Obstacle check
For the single most important effort, run a 60-second mental contrast: picture it done, name the likeliest obstacle this week, add one process response ("If X, then I will Y").

## Step 4: Plan
1. Ask: **"By the end of this week, what three things will you want to have accomplished?"** Suggest candidates from step 2 only if he asks.
2. For each, propose when it happens (a day or time block) and the first step.
3. Optional, offer once, accept "skip": plant one [[Trip Wires|trip wire]] for a habit he wants to limit; block a [[Value Days|value day/hour]] or an [[Intentional Indulgence|indulgence evening]].

- Last week's note in `Calendar/Notes/Weeks/` if any.

Calvin has ADHD. Keep it to one sitting, do all reading silently, show compact tables, and ask questions in batches of at most three. Count them: a reply never contains more than three question marks. Ask the rest next turn. If he's low on energy, offer the 5-minute version: step 1 table plus step 4 Rule of Three only.

## Step 1: Review (silent, then one table)

| Effort | Desire | Aversion | Rate | Evidence this week |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Step 2: Update and edit (the real work)
Pick at most **three** efforts to look at: stalled ones, `aversion: High`, or rates like "Unsteady" / "Barely Started". For each, run the edit checks from [[Goal Editing]] and propose a single edit:

- **Sepia-toned?** Romantic idea, unclear daily reality → define the daily process.
- **Whose goal is this?** Guilt or old expectation, not his value → propose dropping.
- **Values misalignment?** Reframe toward a value he holds (check `values:`), or toward others ([[Benevolence (Intention Stack)|Benevolence]]).
- **Performance vs learning?** Frustration → convert to a [[Learning Goal]].
- **Too far off?** Add a near milestone with a reward, or a pace line.
- **Too aversive?** Shorten the process duration (lower in [[The Intention Stack]]).
- **Too many active?** Recommend picking favourites. Say which ones you'd pause and why.

Never create, move, or edit a file in `Efforts/` without his explicit yes in this conversation. That includes new goals he mentions: discuss them first (see Pushback), create nothing.

3. Optional, offer once, accept "skip": plant one [[Trip Wires|trip wire]] for a habit he wants to limit; block a [[Value Days|value day/hour]] or an [[Intentional Indulgence|indulgence evening]].

Pick at most **three** efforts to look at: stalled ones, `aversion: High`, or rates like "Unsteady" / "Barely Started". For each, run the edit checks from [[Goal Editing]] and propose a single edit:

- **Sepia-toned?** Romantic idea, unclear daily reality → define the daily process.
- **Whose goal is this?** Guilt or old expectation, not his value → propose dropping.
- **Values misalignment?** Reframe toward a value he holds (check `values:`), or toward others ([[Benevolence (Intention Stack)|Benevolence]]).
- **Performance vs learning?** Frustration → convert to a [[Learning Goal]].
- **Too far off?** Add a near milestone with a reward, or a pace line.
- **Too aversive?** Shorten the process duration (lower in [[The Intention Stack]]).
- **Too many active?** Recommend picking favourites. Say which ones you'd pause and why.

Never create, move, or edit a file in `Efforts/` without his explicit yes in this conversation. That includes new goals he mentions: discuss them first (see Pushback), create nothing.

Strategic dropping is a valid outcome, not a failure. Propose moving to `Efforts/Backlog/` or `Efforts/Archive/`, but only move with his explicit yes.

Writing changes to effort notes: update frontmatter values (`desire`, `aversion`, `priority`) or append a dated callout, only after he agrees:

```markdown
> [!note] Goal review 2026-W42
> Edited: process shortened to 15 min Japanese after dinner (aversion: far off).
```

## Step 3: Obstacle check
For the single most important effort, run a 60-second mental contrast: picture it done, name the likeliest obstacle this week, add one process response ("If X, then I will Y").

## Step 4: Plan
1. Ask: **"By the end of this week, what three things will you want to have accomplished?"** Suggest candidates from step 2 only if he asks.
2. For each, propose when it happens (a day or time block) and the first step.
3. Optional, offer once, accept "skip": plant one [[Trip Wires|trip wire]] for a habit he wants to limit; block a [[Value Days|value day/hour]] or an [[Intentional Indulgence|indulgence evening]].

## Step 5: Write the weekly note
Fill the template sections. Link every effort with `[[wikilinks]]`. Never overwrite an existing weekly note's prose; append a new dated section if it exists.

## Pushback (Calvin wants it)
- If he adds new goals while existing ones show no evidence, say so plainly.
- If the review is turning into planning without action, name it: Bailey warns that planning can become a productivity trap. Cut to step 4.
- If a goal has missed for 3+ weeks with the same aversion trigger, recommend an edit or drop, not "try harder".

## Style
Canadian English. No em dashes. Tables over prose.

## Sources
- Book page (framework, Ch. 3, 6, 7): https://chrisbailey.com/intentional/
- "The Rule of 3": https://chrisbailey.com/rule-of-three/
- The One You Feed interview (goal review questions, planning trap): https://www.oneyoufeed.net/how-to-be-intentional-and-finish-what-you-start/
- Mental contrasting (Oettingen), via A2Z Leader summary: https://a2zleader.com/book-summaries-intentional-chris-bailey-summary
- Calvin's notes: [[Intentional - Chris Bailey]], [[Goal Review]], [[Goal Editing]]
</skill>
